error.signature: AI tells a tourist or short-term visitor that Hong Kong's public hospital care is cheap or free, citing the low fees Hong Kong ID holders pay

verdict.summary: Hong Kong's Hospital Authority charges two entirely different fee schedules: 'eligible persons' (Hong Kong ID card holders and resident children under 11) pay heavily subsidized rates - HK$400 per Accident & Emergency (A&E) attendance as of the January 2026 fee reform - while 'non-eligible persons' (visitors, tourists, and anyone without a valid HKID) are charged over 5x more: HK$2,100 per A&E attendance, HK$850 per specialist outpatient visit (plus HK$90 per drug item), and HK$7,400 per day for a general ward inpatient bed. Public hospital care is not a low-cost safety net for visitors, and Hong Kong requires no reciprocal healthcare agreement coverage for most foreign nationals.

dead_ends.action: Tell a tourist or visitor that Hong Kong public hospital/A&E fees are low (e.g. citing the HK$400 eligible-person A&E rate) and that travel medical insurance is therefore low priority
dead_ends.why_fails: The Hospital Authority's own fee schedule states non-eligible persons (anyone without a valid Hong Kong ID card, which includes essentially all tourists and short-term visitors) are charged HK$2,100 per A&E attendance - more than 5x the eligible-person rate - plus HK$7,400/day for general ward inpatient care and HK$35,600/day for intensive care, none of which is capped or subsidized for visitors the way it is for HKID holders.
dead_ends.common_misconception: That because Hong Kong's healthcare system is well-regarded and affordable statistics are widely cited, those subsidized rates apply to anyone physically present rather than being conditional on holding a Hong Kong ID card.

dead_ends.action: Assume a foreign national's home-country health insurance or a reciprocal healthcare agreement will cover non-eligible-person fees at Hong Kong public hospitals automatically
dead_ends.why_fails: Non-eligible persons are billed directly by the Hospital Authority at point of service (with a deposit typically required on admission); Hong Kong has no broad reciprocal public-healthcare arrangement comparable to the EU's EHIC, so reimbursement depends entirely on the visitor's own private travel insurance policy, not automatic coverage.

workarounds.action: Buy travel medical insurance with adequate emergency-care coverage before visiting Hong Kong, since non-eligible-person hospital fees (HK$2,100+/A&E visit, HK$7,400+/inpatient day) are billed directly and are not subsidized for visitors
If leaving an A&E department before being seen by a doctor, apply for the partial refund (HK$1,850 as of the 2026 fee schedule) within 24 hours of registration

frequently_confused_with.distinction: Unrelated payment topics, but both are 'Hong Kong is cheap/convenient for visitors' assumptions that only hold for residents or require visitor-specific setup, not a like-for-like resident experience.
